claim: A choice question reads its keys, not their descriptions: whatever the planner should weigh about a card must be in the key, which is why the bot writes card notes there.
evidence: Tests before the loop: replayed picks did not change at all when a note was added to the description; Laya took a new weapon in 4 of 6 offers once the key said so.

claim: The decision models judge one concrete option at a time better than they rank many at once, so each goal and each move is its own question.
evidence: Tests before the loop, on replayed states; the bot is built around it.

claim: Words beat numbers: describing a move's cost as 'Tibo would get badly hurt' picks the least damaging move far more often than a percentage.
evidence: Tests before the loop, Laya on 50 replayed states: a move within 2% of the least damaging one 90% of the time with words, 80% with 'would lose N%', 38% with the number alone.

claim: A danger rating tracks how many threats a description lists, not which ones, so a fatal move with a short description can rate safest.
evidence: Tests before the loop: Laya rated a fatal move safest in 4 of 8 replayed states, and stood in hot oil forecast 'very badly hurt' for ten seconds while every step out was 'scratched'. The bot therefore never offers moves the forecast prices clearly worse.

claim: A 0-4 hurt score per move finds the least damaging move more reliably than a yes/no danger question.
evidence: Tests before the loop, Jev on replayed Nightmare steps: 98-100% with the score against 95% with yes/no.

claim: The decision models weigh the start of a text most: what matters goes first.
evidence: Seen while writing the bot's move descriptions; never measured. 2026-11-07_16-51-16 put the directive first and the planner followed it for chests, which agrees but does not isolate position.

claim: On the Nightmare Daily, crowds barely hurt a Tibo that keeps moving; nearly all damage comes from hot oil and bosses.
evidence: 2026-11-07_15-44-50 (18:20, seed DG0S-Z730R0): hot oil 274 and bosses 481 of 773 damage; blight-spore 14 and Spore vent 4 are the rest. enemies_near was 0 on almost every row, including 800 around and 0 within 60 at 17:09, and 799 around at 18:20. One run.

claim: With no directive, the planner evades through the first minute and then collects gems, and a boss on screen usually does not replace that goal.
evidence: 2026-11-07_15-44-50: evade re-picked from 0:05 to 1:13 aside from a 3-second explore at 1:02; gems won from 1:21 on. Amusing stayed a chest through contact at 2:08 (hp 105 to 57). Deep Freezer, Wireworm, Strawman, Mandoline and Grater Golem stayed gems. Compost Titan at 17:03 is the exception: gems were dropped for evade. One run. 2026-11-07_16-36-04 (nightmare-1 world, seed 2R6JH5): the same templates, with no directive, evaded from 0:00 and never started gems. Gems peaked at 42% at 1:06, one point behind explore down-right. enemies_near was 4 by 0:08 and often above 0, unlike the daily rows at 0. Died at 3:16 still evading (22 evade starts, 0 gems). Contradicts the gems half off the daily. One world sample.

New cards won when higher (Potato Rain 50% at 0:48, Hash Brown Shield 57% at 1:45, Gravy Heart 67% at 1:57, Starch Chain 40% at 3:37). Reroll lost at 4% and at 29%. No recipe finished. Fourth run, upgrade half only.
